verdicts.reviewer_notes: Second-round review. WebFetch could not parse the signed PDF (gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/FINAL-N-9-26-AI-EO-9.18.26-SIGNED.pdf), but the saved binary was read in full (3 pages) with the Read tool. Verified against the signed text: Executive Order N-9-26, 'to become effective immediately', signed 'this 18th day of September 2026' and attested by the Secretary of State. Para 1: Government Operations Agency (GovOps) to complete Gov. Code 8898.1 requirements and post IVO application requirements by May 1, 2027. Para 2: complete 11549.82(a) and begin 11549.82(b) actions by December 1, 2027. Para 3: GovOps, in consultation with Cal OES, to submit recommendations to the Governor's office by November 16, 2026, covering at least (a) onsite IVOs at all large frontier developers, (b) independent verification of safety frameworks, transparency reports and risk assessments, (c) a 'kill switch' whose efficacy is verified on an ongoing basis by an IVO, and (d) updating the critical safety incident definition to include loss-of-control incidents. The 'no rights or benefits ... enforceable at law or in equity' clause is present. The 23 Sept gov.ca.gov release (dated Sep 23, 2026) confirms the four recommendation topics. It names no order number or deadlines, and the item does not rely on it for either. event_date 2026-09-18, stage in_force (effective immediately) and confidence high (primary read in full) are all correct. Small nuance: the order asks for recommendations 'addressing the technical feasibility and potential efficacy of amendments', which the summary condenses to 'recommendations ... on amendments'. That is acceptable. Note for the editor: type 'regulation' is a loose fit for a gubernatorial order. ITEM_TYPES has no executive-order value and the protocol does not define item types, so this is not a failed check. Grep of content/items and content/instruments for N-9-26, kill switch and 8898 found no duplicates. The existing item us-ca-sb-813-ab-1405-ai-third-party-verification covers the underlying IVO statutes, not this order.

Second-round review. Three fetches of the cited whitehouse.gov page gave inconsistent extractions. One reproduced Sec. 2 and the first part of Sec. 3 verbatim but omitted the list of what the proposal must include. Another asserted 'conforming amendments' sits in a 'Section 3(b)' but described the structure wrongly. I could not reliably confirm every claim from the cited page alone. I therefore read the Federal Register public-inspection copy of the same document (public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-20321.pdf, read in full). It confirms: EO 14434, 'Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence', signed 'THE WHITE HOUSE, September 29, 2026', FR Doc. 2026-20321 filed 10/1/2026, publication date 10/2/2026. Sec. 2(a): 'To the maximum extent permitted by law', agencies use 'Super Intelligence'/'SI' in official correspondence, public communications, websites, reports, policy documents and other non-statutory documents within the executive branch. Sec. 2(b): previously issued regulations, Presidential actions, contracts, grants and historical documents need not be altered. Sec. 3(a): definition by reference to 15 U.S.C. 9401(3). Sec. 3(b): the APST must submit proposed legislative language within 60 days, and the proposal must include '(ii) any proposed conforming amendments, as appropriate'. The text contains no reference to States, state law or preemption, so 'does not address preemption of state law' is accurate. Sec. 4(c) contains the no-enforceable-rights clause. The summary is accurate, but its 'conforming amendments' claim is verifiable only from the FR copy, which the item does not cite. It is therefore not supported by the item's own sources. Date, stage in_force, tier and tone are fine. No duplicate: grep for 14434 and Super Intelligence found matches only in this run.
required_changes: Add a second source: {"url": "https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-20321.pdf", "publisher": "Office of the Federal Register", "tier": "primary"} with a current accessed_at. This is the full signed text, including Sec. 3(b)(ii) on conforming amendments.
Optionally add to the summary: 'Scheduled for publication in the Federal Register on 2 October 2026 (FR Doc. 2026-20321).'

verdicts.reviewer_notes: Second-round review. Re-fetched the gov.ca.gov release (dated Sep 10, 2026). It says 'Today, Governor Gavin Newsom ... signed', so event_date 2026-09-10 is correct. The release lists 13 bills, including SB 1119 (Padilla, Wicks, Bauer-Kahan) 'Companion chatbots: children's safety', AB 1709 'Covered platforms: age restriction: e-Safety Advisory Commission', SB 1276 'Crimes: sexual exploitation of a child' and AB 1159 'Student personal information'. All four titles and authors match the item. The provision bullets are unattributed checkmark bullets, as the item says. The chatbot bullet reads 'Named after Adam Raine, "Adam's Law" requires robust protections around companion chatbots for children, including crisis protocols in the case of suicidal ideation, parental controls, and notifications should a child disable safety settings', plus 'independent child safety audits and annual risk assessments'. That bullet names Adam's Law rather than SB 1119 by number. The Padilla release (sd18.senate.ca.gov/node/419, dated August 31, 2026, 'Today, California lawmakers passed Adam's Law (SB 1119)', Senate 39-0, Assembly 64-4, heading to the Governor) supplies the link to SB 1119, so the item's attribution holds across its two cited sources. Minor wording point: the governor's release also uses the name 'Adam's Law', not only Padilla's office. This is not an error. Stage 'passed' fits a signed bill whose operative date is unverified. Medium confidence is appropriate given only press releases were read, and the item states that limitation honestly. Tone is neutral, and why_it_matters makes no unsupported claims. Grep for SB 1119, Adam's Law and companion chatbot in content/items and content/instruments found nothing. The existing 30 Sept package item (us-ca-sept-2026-ai-bill-package-signed) is a different signing and does not list SB 1119.

Second-round review. Verified against the signed PDF, which was read in full. Kind executive_order, status in_force ('effective immediately') and the single timeline entry dated 2026-09-18 are correct. All three key_obligations match paras 1-3 of the order. The no-enforceable-rights statement is accurate. One problem is in the summary. 'Accelerates implementation timelines' is the governor's 23 Sept press-release characterisation ('accelerate the implementation timelines for SB 813 and AB 1405'). The order's own text sets deadlines for completing statutory requirements 'as required by law' and never says it accelerates anything. I did not read the statutes' own deadlines, so the claim is unverified. The only source the instrument cites is the PDF, which does not support 'accelerates'. This is promotional framing presented as fact, so claim_matches_source and neutral_tone fail. 'Commissions recommendations on strengthening frontier AI safety law' is also looser than the operative text: recommendations 'addressing the technical feasibility and potential efficacy of amendments to existing state laws regarding AI safety and security'. 'Strengthening' appears only in a WHEREAS clause. No duplicate exists in content/instruments, and grep for N-9-26 found nothing.
required_changes: Replace the summary's first sentence with: 'Gubernatorial order of 18 September 2026 that sets deadlines for the Government Operations Agency to implement California's independent verification organization provisions (Gov. Code 8898.1 by 1 May 2027; 11549.82 by 1 December 2027) and commissions recommendations, due 16 November 2026, on the technical feasibility and potential efficacy of amendments to state AI safety and security law.' Alternatively, if 'accelerates' is kept, attribute it explicitly ('which the Governor's office describes as accelerating...') and add a timeline entry or reference pointing to the 23 Sept gov.ca.gov release.

verdicts.reviewer_notes: Second-round review. The name, kind executive_order, status in_force, the 2026-09-29 timeline date and both key_obligations were verified against the whitehouse.gov page. Its Sec. 2(a) and Sec. 3(b) first sentence were reproduced verbatim in my fetch. They were also verified against the Federal Register public-inspection copy (FR Doc. 2026-20321, signed September 29, 2026, publication 10/2/2026). The summary ('replacing AI terminology with Super Intelligence in federal agency communications and starting a 60 day process for a proposed statutory definition') matches Sec. 2 and 3(b). Unlike the item, the instrument makes no 'conforming amendments' claim, so the cited page supports it. Recommended but not required: add a timeline entry dated 2026-10-02 (stage in_force, note 'Published in the Federal Register, FR Doc. 2026-20321') with source_url https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-20321.pdf or the federalregister.gov/d/2026-20321 URL. Also align last_verified (2026-10-06) with the item's access date (2026-10-07). No duplicate: content/instruments contains us-eo-14365-national-ai-policy-framework, a different order, and nothing for 14434.

Second-round review. Summary claim 'signed 10 September 2026': confirmed by the governor's release ('Today ... signed', dated Sep 10, 2026). Crisis protocols, parental controls, notifications on disabling safety settings, independent audits and annual risk assessments all match the governor's release text. Key obligations attributed to Padilla were all confirmed on sd18.senate.ca.gov/node/419. Audit findings are 'submitted to the California Attorney General'. The incident reporting mechanism is 'overseen by the Attorney General'. The private right of action covers 'crisis referral services, parental notice, default protections, and prohibitions on harmful outputs'. Timeline entry 2026-08-31: the Padilla release, dated August 31, 2026, says 'Today, California lawmakers passed Adam's Law (SB 1119)', with Senate 39-0 and Assembly 64-4, sent to the Governor. Timeline entry 2026-09-10 matches the governor's release. Kind statute and status passed (signed, operative date unverified) are correct. The summary discloses that operative dates were not verified. Small inconsistency, not a failure: the governor's release says 'annual risk assessments', while Padilla describes risk assessments before release of new or substantially modified chatbots. The key obligation keeps 'annual', which is the governor's wording, so it is not wrong, but the chaptered text should settle it later. No duplicate in content/instruments.
